**ADMIRAL’S BRIEFING – 2130 HOURS, NIGHT BEFORE D-DAY**  
**Fleet Operations Center, USS *Yelp Resolution***

*(The admiral strides onto the steel decking. Every boot heel cracks like a 5-inch gun. The fleet is assembled in perfect ranks: captains, commanders, JAG officers, review moderators, and one very salty petty officer holding a printed copy of the disputed 1-star review. Lights snap to battle stations red. The admiral does not smile.)*

**“ATTEN-TION!”**

Sailors… tomorrow we sail into the narrow strait known as **“Yelp Dispute Resolution.”**

For forty-three days the enemy has occupied our five-star waters. A lone, disgruntled quartermaster third class wrote a review so foul it dropped our aggregate from 4.8 to 4.3 and made our Google listing look like a floating rust bucket. He called our calamari “rubbery,” our service “slower than a Monday in the yard,” and—most unforgivable—claimed our maître d’ “had the personality of a bilge pump.”

**This will not stand.**

Tonight we rehearse the operation. Listen up, because I will say this once:

**PHASE ONE – RECONNAISSANCE**  
At 0600 our intelligence team will re-upload every timestamped photo, every signed credit-card receipt, every security-cam still showing the gentleman in question pounding his third complimentary bread basket while complaining the bread was “too crusty.” We will bury him in documented excellence.

**PHASE TWO – COUNTER-BATTERY FIRE**  
Our crack team of former JAG review ninjas will draft a response so calm, so professional, so devastatingly polite that civilians reading it will feel the sudden urge to stand at attention. It will begin with “We are truly sorry your experience fell short of the USS *Hospitality* standard…” and it will end with the quiet implication that his palate was issued by the lowest bidder.

**PHASE THREE – THE SURGE**  
Every satisfied customer who ever left a glowing review will receive a single, dignified request: “If our service met the highest traditions of the Naval Service, would you kindly make that known again?” We expect a tsunami of five-star reinforcements by 1100.
